main_conclusion: Most plausible BF16 failure is sequence-row-shape-dependent finite-precision drift in DenseXAttn and decoder projections/attention when incremental decode changes M from a whole prefix to1. The exact first divergent operation is NOT measured. Current source has consistent cache positions, length/mask handling and token-local bridge insertion. NF4 cached decoding remains unqualified and has an additional concrete row-dependent kernel dispatch.

confirmed_source_trace.fact: The native generator encodes the board once, installs16 pre-layer hooks at decoder layers0,2,...30, and removes every handle. Cached generation sends only next_token and prior KV; the attention mask grows by1. No-cache generation resends the full prefix.

DenseXAttn uses per-token LayerNorm, projections and FFN; attention covers64 fixed board positions with eval dropout0. Decoder token rows never attend to other decoder rows inside the bridge. No sequence-global normalization or changing board conditioning was found.

SmolLM3Model derives position_ids=arange(current_length)+past_key_values.get_seq_length(). The config has36 full-attention layers and no sliding window. Blindly adding the removed Transformers4 cache_position API would not address this installed5.19 path.
DynamicLayer appends keys and values with torch.cat on the sequence axis. get_mask_sizes returns past+query. The all-one attention mask in the native loop covers that combined length.

For all-one inputs, _ignore_causal_mask_sdpa skips the explicit mask when q=1 or q=kv. sdpa_attention_forward sets is_causal=False for q=1 and True for full-prefix q>1. This is correct last-row geometry by source; actual masks and positions were not retained by failedv5.

The math profile disables reduced BF16 GEMM reductions and TF32, and requests math SDPA with FP32 intermediates. It does not convert every BF16 projection output or activation to FP32. Shape-dependent projection arithmetic remains possible.

Installed bitsandbytes0.50.2 Linear4bit calls matmul_4bit, whose CUDA dispatch chooses raw custom cgemm or dequantize+F.linear based on M,N,K and the device. M=1 always selects custom in this heuristic; a full prefix may use the fallback. PyTorch matmul flags cannot be assumed to control a raw bitsandbytes C kernel.

plain_cpu_probe.summary: No framework imports. Plain mathematical full-prefix last-row attention equals cached q=1 noncausal attention; the naive upper-left causal mask differs. The exact installed dispatch function ran ONLY with stub dtype/device properties (84 SMs, SM120). It selected M=1 custom versus M=84/85 fallback for q/k/v/o/down, and custom for up/gate. Device properties are authored, not measured. This demonstrates conditional code paths, not hardware output drift or latency.

ranked_hypotheses.hypothesis: Row-shape-dependent BF16 arithmetic in bridge norm_y/W_Q/FFN, decoder QKV/MLP projections, or SDPA. Cached prefix keys preserve prefill rounding; full-prefix recomputation can round earlier token rows differently.
ranked_hypotheses.support: No-cache manual/native equality is exact at all4 tested prefixes. The source has consistent token-local conditioning and causal bookkeeping. Cached outputs are finite and all3 top tokens match, but numerical limits fail.
ranked_hypotheses.uncertainty: The exact first divergent operation is unmeasured. The receipt lacks per-layer tensors and a cached-flag versus no-cache prefill comparison. No repair success is claimed.

lower_risk_latency_option.idea: Cache each frozen bridge board-side norm_x/W_K/W_V once per request while keepingdecoder no_cache.
lower_risk_latency_option.reason: The encoded board and frozen bridge weights are constant within a request. Board K/V projection inputs always have64 rows, independently of decoder sequence length. Current DenseXAttn recomputes32 board-side K/V projections across16 bridges on every decoder forward.
lower_risk_latency_option.scope: Request-local only: never reuse across boards, history, dtype, encoder or bridge identities. The16 bridges x2 K/V tensors x64 squares x2048 width x2 BF16 bytes require8,388,608bytes (8MiB), excluding temporaries.
